intended_object: The constant diagram, indexed by the open normal subgroups of the profinite group G, whose value at every level is the compact Hausdorff group of total invariants A^G and whose transition maps are all identities. It is the middle term of the finite Tate norm row (from the docstring and the module documentation).
explanation:
The body sends every object to `group A L ⊤`. That is `openSubgroupInvariants A ⊤`, i.e. A^G, with its chosen compact Hausdorff topology, packaged as a `CompHausAddCommGrp`. Every morphism goes to `𝟙 _`, and the functor laws hold by `rfl`/`simp`. So this is exactly the constant functor `(Functor.const (OpenNormalSubgroup G)).obj (group A L ⊤)`, written out by hand. That matches the docstring ("identity transition at every deflation level") and the module's description of "the constant diagram of compact total invariants".

Writing it out instead of using `Functor.const` gives the same object, so it is not an error. It is also not too narrow: it is one particular diagram, and the setting (profinite G, compact level topologies) is the one the surrounding Tate norm construction is built on. The natural transformations `compactFiniteTateNorm` and `compactFiniteTateZeroProjection` use it consistently: the norm maps from S-coinvariants land in A^G, and the quotient map goes out of A^G.
